findings.quote: convinced that if he could throw them into confusion he would then sail the rest of the way safely
findings.problem: Greek: πεπεισμένος καταταχήσειν καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν ἀσφαλῶς ἤδη κομισθήσεσθαι. καταταχήσειν means he would get ahead of / outstrip them by speed; nothing about throwing the enemy into confusion.
findings.proposed_fix: convinced that he would get the start of them and then sail the rest of the way safely

findings.problem: Greek: σὺν δὲ τούτοις ἄφρακτα *** — a number is missing after ἄφρακτα (lacuna); the English reads on as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: besides undecked ships [number lost in the Greek text]

findings.quote: because the enemy vessel had a high-built prow
findings.problem: Greek: ἀναστείρου τῆς νεὼς οὔσης — the genitive absolute does not name whose ship had the raised stem; the sense (he took the blow above the waterline) favors his own ship, the opposite of the English assignment. Ambiguous, so preserve the ambiguity.
findings.proposed_fix: because the ship's stem was raised (the Greek does not say whose ship)

findings.quote: but he struck the enemy below the waterline
findings.problem: Greek: τὴν δὲ τῶν πολεμίων τρώσας ναῦν ὑπὸ τὰ * βίαχα — the text is corrupt/defective (asterisk, and βίαχα is not a known word); 'below the waterline' is an invented smoothing.
findings.proposed_fix: but he struck the enemy ship under the [text corrupt: ὑπὸ τὰ * βίαχα]

units.note: Corrupt passage in Deinocrates' clash; no certain restoration.

findings.quote: Philip had the advantage in the number of his light craft, but Attalus had the advantage in the number of decked ships.
findings.problem: Greek: καθ᾽ ὅσον … ἐπλεόναζον οἱ παρὰ τοῦ Φιλίππου λέμβοι, κατὰ τοσοῦτον διέφερον οἱ περὶ τὸν Ἄτταλον τῷ τῶν καταφράκτων νεῶν πλήθει — a proportional correlative: by just as much as Philip's light boats were more numerous, by so much Attalus' side excelled in decked ships (the two balanced, hence ἐφάμιλλος). The English drops the correlation.
findings.proposed_fix: For in proportion as Philip's light boats were more numerous, by just so much did Attalus' side excel in the number of decked ships.

units.note: All numbers checked against the Greek.
